leagues.name: Asian Tour
notes: The 2026 season is the 31st of the modern Asian Tour; the Wikipedia 2026 schedule table (fetched 25 Sep 2026) lists 17 official events including 2 cancelled International Series events (International Series India, International Series China); asiantour.com schedule pages are JavaScript-rendered and returned no table text.

On 21 July 2026 the Asian Tour left its LIV Golf partnership and joined the PGA Tour / DP World Tour strategic alliance with immediate effect; the DP World Tour returns to co-sanctioning Asian Tour events from 2027 (CBS Sports, 2026-07-21). AFP (via Philstar, 2026-07-22) reports the partnership runs until at least 2029 and that LIV Golf had bankrolled the International Series to the tune of $300m.

After the split, remaining events lost International Series event status (Wikipedia notes 'Tournament had International Series event status removed following the restructuring of LIV Golf after the Public Investment Fund's announcement of withdrawal of funding', citing Flushing It, 2026-08-15); the three late-season events (Link Hong Kong Open, BingoPlus Philippine Open, PIF Saudi International) carry an 'International Series [status removed]' footnote.

The International Series pages on internationalseries.com still describe the 2026 season as co-sanctioned by LIV Golf and the Asian Tour with a pathway to LIV Golf (fetched 25 Sep 2026); they may predate the July 2026 split - flagged in unsourced.

Event-host shape: tournaments are recorded as clubs (sportId golf, leagueId asian-tour) following the dp-world-tour pattern; kits array is empty; tournament sponsors are recorded as clubId-null league-partner deals (org-partner shape).

deals.note: PIF-funded LIV Golf partnered with the Asian Tour from the league's 2022 launch, creating and funding the International Series; the partnership ended when the Asian Tour joined the PGA Tour / DP World Tour strategic alliance on 21 July 2026 (CBS Sports). AFP via Philstar (2026-07-22) reports LIV had bankrolled the International Series to the tune of $300m, and that PIF announced earlier in 2026 it would stop funding LIV after the 2026 season. Existing claim liv-pif-funding covers the PIF-LIV funding.

PIF is the title sponsor - the event carries its name ('Title sponsor of the PIF Saudi International', internationalseries.com partners page, fetched 2026-09-25). Event: Nov 18-21, 2026, Riyadh Golf Club, USD 5m purse (internationalseries.com event page). Wikipedia's 2026 table notes the event's International Series status was removed after the LIV restructuring. PIF has title-sponsored the event since 2022 per the site's lead (lead only - primary start date not verified).

claims.text: The Asian Tour had been in partnership with LIV Golf since the league's 2022 launch, with the PIF-funded International Series as a key part of LIV's promotion and relegation; on 21 July 2026 the PGA Tour and DP World Tour announced the partnership would extend to the Asian Tour with immediate effect, ending the LIV arrangement, with DP World Tour returning to co-sanction Asian Tour events from 2027.
claims.short: Asian Tour ended its LIV Golf partnership and joined the PGA/DP World Tour alliance on 21 July 2026.

claims.text: LIV Golf has been bankrolling the Asian Tour's International Series to the tune of $300 million, leaving the future of the elevated events - each offering $2 million in prize money and a pathway to LIV - in doubt after the Asian Tour's partnership with the PGA and DP World Tours; the Asian Tour said its priority was to maintain the International Series events planned for later in 2026 'in some form'.
claims.short: LIV put about $300m into the International Series; its future was left in doubt by the split.

claims.text: The PIF Saudi International (Nov 18-21, 2026, Riyadh Golf Club, USD 5m purse) is title-sponsored by PIF and presented/powered by SoftBank Investment Advisers; the International Series site still describes it as the Series finale whose rankings determine LIV Golf promotion spots, wording that may predate the July 2026 LIV-Asian Tour split.
claims.short: PIF titles and SoftBank Investment Advisers presents the Saudi International, the $5m season finale.

source.name: The International Series - PIF Saudi International event page and Partners page

proposedRatings.reasoning: PIF is the Saudi sovereign wealth fund chaired by the Crown Prince; it funded LIV Golf's takeover of the Asian Tour's International Series (about $300m per AFP) and titles the tour's flagship Saudi International. Saudi state money on the tour: the HRW-recorded execution surge (322+ by Dec 2025) supports serious, consistent with the existing serious rating logic for PIF elsewhere on the site; severe is reserved for live armed conflict.

All from the Wikipedia 2026 Asian Tour schedule table (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Asian_Tour, fetched 25 Sep 2026, citing asiantour.com), purses in local currency where shown: Philippine Golf Championship (Philippines, 8 Feb, USD 500,000, new tournament, winner Cho Woo-young); New Zealand Open (New Zealand, 1 Mar, NZD 2m, co-sanctioned ANZ PGA Tour of Australasia, winner Daniel Hillier); International Series Japan (5 Apr, USD 2m, winner Travis Smyth); Singapore Open (26 Apr, USD 2m, winner Ham Jeong-woo); GS Caltex Maekyung Open (South Korea, 3 May, KRW 1.3bn, co-sanctioned Korean Tour, winner Song Min-hyuk); Taiwan Glass Taifong Open (Taiwan, 10 May, winner Ian Snyman); Kolon Korea Open (24 May, KRW 1.4bn, winner Yang Ji-ho); Am Green IGPL Bharath Classic Morocco (7 Jun, USD 500,000, co-sanctioned IGPL, winner Charlie Lindh); International Series Morocco (14 Jun, USD 2m, winner Kho Taichi); Yeangder Tournament Players Championship (Taiwan, 20 Sep, USD 1.2m, winner Pavit Tangkamolprasert); Mercuries Taiwan Masters (27 Sep, USD 1.2m); SJM Macao Open (18 Oct, USD 1m); International Series India (11 Oct) and International Series China (8 Nov) both cancelled; BingoPlus Philippine Open (15 Nov, USD 2m); PIF Saudi International (21 Nov, USD 5m).

Title sponsors embedded in event names but not separately verified against a sponsor announcement: GS Caltex (Korean refining JV of GS Group and Caltex), Taiwan Glass (Taiwan Glass Industry Corp), Kolon (Kolon Group), Yeangder (Taiwanese property group), Mercuries (Taiwanese Mercuries Group), SJM (Macau gaming operator SJM Resorts/HK-listed SJM Holdings), New Zealand Open co-sanctioning partner ANZ. Each needs a primary source before a sponsor row.

The 2026 event count: the Wikipedia table lists 17 events (15 scheduled + 2 cancelled International Series events); one earlier fetch summary reported 15-16, so the reviewer should re-check against asiantour.com once its schedule renders (asiantour.com is JavaScript-rendered and returned no table text on 25 Sep 2026).

International Series pages (internationalseries.com, fetched 25 Sep 2026) still describe the 2026 season as 'co-sanctioned by LIV Golf and the Asian Tour' with a LIV pathway and label the PIF Saudi International the Series finale; Wikipedia notes International Series status was removed from remaining events after the PIF/LIV withdrawal, so the site text may predate the July 2026 split - confirm the final sanction of the Nov events.

The Link Hong Kong Open title-sponsor identity: the International Series partners page lists LINK with sponsor-block id 'link-reit', i.e. Link Asset Management/Link REIT; Link REIT's own site was searched but no press release naming the golf tournament was found on linkreit.com - the title-sponsorship claim rests on the IS partners page.

Philstar/AFP reports the new PGA/DP World/Asian Tour partnership runs 'until at least 2029'; the CBS article gives no end date; the joint statement itself was not directly accessible from this environment (apnews.com returned 403).

NGAP (National Golf Association of the Philippines) is listed on the International Series partners page as 'Partner of the BingoPlus Philippine Open'; it is a governing body, not a commercial sponsor, so no sponsor row was created.
